title: Strings: Hashing, KMP / Z-function, Trie (Depth Pass)
relevance: High — second wave after CSES String Matching / Borders / Periods, Password, Good Substrings, Compress Words, and binary-trie Vasiliy; these hide period constraints, hash-equality trees, trie DP, and KMP-on-compressed / KMP+DP rather than announcing the template.
company_notes: Autocomplete / dictionary decode — Spy Syndrome / Color with Occurrences / A Lot of Games: trie over a word list, sometimes reversed or as a game on missing letters. Split / validate a serial with modular checks — Hacking Cypher / Check Transcription: rolling numeric or block hashes under format constraints (OA-flavoured). Count strings containing a password / virus — Required Substring / Obsessive String / Lucky Common Subsequence: DP on the KMP failure state. Nearly periodic / one typo — Nearly Shortest Repeating / Spelling Check / Watto: period or Hamming-1 membership, common timed-OA twist on plain matching.

phases.goal: Spot depth-pass string asks that hide π/period constraints, hash-equality trees, trie DP, KMP-on-compressed, or KMP+DP rather than announcing the template.

must_hit.point: After the famous set, contests stop saying “run KMP” and leave a border/period invariant, a dictionary of fragments to glue, a one-mismatch query, or a tiny automaton state.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one of those hidden asks instead of a plain “find pattern” cue.

must_hit.point: Spot it when n≤10^6 forces linear string tools, when “exactly one change / one deletion” appears, when answers are counts of strings containing a pattern, or when a dictionary is searched backwards.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites n≤10^6, one change/deletion, pattern-containing counts, or reverse dictionary search as the depth signal.

must_hit.point: Depth-pass states still look like “compare substrings”, “longest prefix that is also suffix”, or “walk a trie”, but the extra work is non-obvious (forced placements via π, reverse-trie decoding, even-split hash classes, run-length KMP, automaton DP, or binary-trie XOR counts).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates the surface wording from one of those non-obvious extras.

must_hit.point: “Nearly periodic / one typo” OA twists (period with ≤1 mismatch per block, one deletion, Hamming distance 1 membership) are upgrades on plain matching, not full edit distance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties Nearly Shortest Repeating / Spelling Check / Watto-style asks to period or Hamming-1 tools.

probes: What in the statement says this is forced placements, reverse-trie decode, even-split equivalence, KMP automaton DP, run-length KMP, or one-mismatch hashing rather than template KMP/trie?
When does n≤10^6 or “exactly one change / one deletion” force a linear string tool instead of nested compares?

hints.1: Look past “run KMP / walk a trie” — ask what invariant or extra state is hidden.
hints.2: Border/period, glue dictionary fragments, one mismatch, reverse search, or count-containing-pattern are the depth signals.
hints.3: Say: n≤10^6 or one change/deletion → linear hash/Z/KMP; reverse dictionary → reverse trie; count strings with a pattern → KMP automaton DP; nearly periodic → period+hash.

phases.goal: Pick the right depth model from the must-internalize checklist: π overlaps, reverse trie, even-split hash, KMP DP, run-length KMP, one-mismatch probes, binary-trie counts, or Z reconstruct.

must_hit.point: Forced placements + π: when several starts of p are required inside s, an overlap is legal iff p’s border chain / period divides the gap; free cells then contribute 26^cnt (Tavas and Malekas).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States π/period legality on gaps and 26^cnt on free cells.

must_hit.point: KMP automaton DP: state = current match length in π; transitions on alphabet; absorb / forbid / require a pattern (Required Substring, Lucky Common Subsequence, Obsessive String).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps π-match length as DP state for require/forbid/count asks.

must_hit.point: Reverse trie decoding: store dictionary words reversed; DP from the end of the ciphertext, walking the trie forward = matching a word ending here (Spy Syndrome 2).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds the trie on reversed words and DP-decodes from the end.

must_hit.point: Even-split equivalence: a∼b if a=b or both even-length and halves equivalent in either order — hash both half-orders, recurse (Equivalent Strings); do not expand into O(n) copies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Hashes both half-orders / recurses and refuses materializing all copies.

must_hit.point: Run-length KMP: compress (c,len) blocks; match the interior exactly, treat the first/last block as a prefix/suffix length constraint (Messenger).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Matches compressed blocks with exact middle and end length constraints.

must_hit.point: One-mismatch / one-delete probes: fix the differing position (or branch once in a trie); compare the two surrounding segments with O(1) hashes (Spelling Check, Watto).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Fixes one branch/position and O(1)-hash-compares the flanks.

must_hit.point: Binary trie counts, not only max: for “XOR ≥ k”, walk bit-by-bit and add whole subtrees when the bit choice already satisfies the threshold (Beautiful Subarrays).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Counts qualifying subtrees on the XOR≥k walk, not only max XOR.

must_hit.point: Z for reconstruct / lex build: Z on A+B and B+A (ABCBAC) or Z from each index (Erase and Extend / Compress String) replaces nested string compares under n≤10^6.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses Z (or hash) instead of nested compares at large n.

probes: Given required starts of p inside s, how do you validate overlaps and count free cells?
When do you keep π-state in DP versus building a reverse trie or hashing even halves?

hints.1: Match the ask to one checklist trick, not generic KMP/trie.
hints.2: π gaps + 26^cnt; reverse words + end DP; both half-orders; π DP state; (c,len) KMP; one branch + O(1) hash; XOR≥k subtree adds; Z/hash not O(n^2) compares.
hints.3: Say: forced starts → π legality then 26^cnt; require/forbid pattern → automaton DP; Spy Syndrome → reverse trie; Equivalent Strings → hash both half-orders; Messenger → run-length KMP; Spelling/Watto → one probe + O(1) hashes; Beautiful Subarrays → count path; ABCBAC/Erase → Z.

phases.goal: Encode π-overlap checks, reverse-trie DP, even-split hashes, automaton transitions, run-length matching, one-mismatch probes, and XOR≥k trie walks correctly.

must_hit.point: Forced placements: check each required overlap of p via the border chain / period before filling; then raise 26^cnt over unmarked free cells.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches π-based overlap reject then free-cell exponentiation.

must_hit.point: KMP automaton DP: state is current π match length; on each alphabet transition follow failure links; absorb when the pattern is completed (require/forbid/count variants).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes state = match length and transitions that can mark absorb/forbid.

must_hit.point: Reverse trie: insert reversed dictionary words; from ciphertext end, walk the trie forward to take a word ending at the current position (Spy Syndrome 2).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Inserts reversed words and DP-walks from the end.

must_hit.point: Even-split: for even lengths, hash both orders of each half and recurse; never expand into O(n) concrete rearrangements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares hashes of both half-orders without materializing copies.

must_hit.point: One-mismatch / one-delete: branch once (or fix the dropped index) and verify left/right segments with O(1) prefix/suffix hashes — not full edit distance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses two surrounding hash equals after one branch/deletion.

must_hit.point: Binary trie XOR≥k: insert prefix XORs; on query walk bits and add whole subtree counts when the chosen bit already meets the threshold.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds subtree sizes on the ≥k side, same structure as Vasiliy but a count query.

probes: How do you implement the π overlap check and 26^cnt free cells for forced placements?
How does the KMP automaton state transition, and how does a one-delete probe use O(1) hashes?

hints.1: Implementation is checklist bookkeeping: π, trie direction, hash orders, automaton state.
hints.2: Validate gaps with π; DP on match length; reverse inserts; hash both halves; one branch + flank hashes; XOR trie adds subtrees.
hints.3: π divides gap then 26^cnt; state=π length with absorb/forbid; reverse words + end DP; both half-order hashes; O(1) flank hashes after one fix; walk bits adding qualifying subtrees.

phases.goal: Justify linear string tools under n≤10^6 and refuse O(n^2) compares / O(n) even-split expansions.

must_hit.point: Under n≤10^6, nested string compares are unacceptable; use Z or hashing (Message Transmission hard, Erase and Extend, Compress String, ABCBAC).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects O(n^2) compares and names Z/hash as the linear tool.

must_hit.point: Even-split equivalence must hash both half-orders and recurse — do not expand into O(n) copies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the O(n)-copies blowup as forbidden.

must_hit.point: One-mismatch / one-delete checks compare surrounding segments with O(1) hashes after fixing the differing position or single trie branch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites O(1) hash segment compares, not rescanning whole strings naively each time.

probes: Why does n≤10^6 rule out nested string compares here?
What goes wrong if you expand every even-split equivalence into concrete copies?

hints.1: Complexity fails are O(n^2) compares or materializing rearrangements.
hints.2: Z/hash for large n; hash both half-orders; O(1) flank hashes after one probe.
hints.3: Cite n≤10^6 → Z/hash not O(n^2) compares; even-split → no O(n) copies; one delete/mismatch → O(1) hash flanks.

phases.goal: Catch depth-pass failure modes: edit-distance overkill, forward-only tries, max-only XOR tries, illegal forced overlaps, and char-level KMP on runs.

must_hit.point: Treating Spelling Check / one-deletion as full edit distance instead of prefix/suffix hash equality after dropping one index.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects edit DP and names one-index drop + hash equals.

must_hit.point: Accepting forced pattern placements that overlap illegally — must check via π / period before counting 26^cnt free cells.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires border-chain legality on gaps before the free-cell exponent.

must_hit.point: Building a forward dictionary trie for Spy Syndrome-style decode instead of reversed words with DP from the end.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags wrong trie direction and missing end-based DP.

must_hit.point: Answering XOR ≥ k with a binary trie that only tracks max XOR — must count path / add qualifying subtrees (Beautiful Subarrays).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes count-on-threshold from Vasiliy-style max query.

must_hit.point: Running character-level KMP on Messenger instead of KMP on run-length (c,len) blocks with exact middle and prefix/suffix end constraints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names compressed-block matching with end length constraints.

must_hit.point: Expanding Equivalent Strings even-splits into O(n) copies, or using O(n^2) string compares under n≤10^6.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags both blowups and points to hash/Z.

probes: What’s wrong with edit distance for one deletion, or max-only XOR for ≥ k counts?
Where do candidates fail forced placements or Messenger-style compressed matching?

hints.1: Depth bugs ignore the checklist extras.
hints.2: One-index hash not edit DP; π before 26^cnt; reverse trie; count not only max; run-length KMP; no O(n)/O(n^2) expansions.
hints.3: Drop one index + O(1) hashes; π-legal gaps then 26^cnt; reverse words + end DP; XOR≥k subtree counts; (c,len) KMP; hash both halves / Z under n≤10^6.

tradeoffs.topic: O(1) hash one-delete / one-mismatch probes vs full edit distance
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Fix the differing position (or branch once in a trie) and compare the two surrounding segments with O(1) hashes (Spelling Check, Watto) — not full edit distance.

tradeoffs.topic: Hash both even half-orders vs expanding O(n) copies
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For Equivalent Strings, a∼b if equal or both even-length with halves equivalent in either order — hash both half-orders and recurse; do not expand into O(n) copies.

tradeoffs.topic: Z/hash under n≤10^6 vs nested string compares
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Z on A+B and B+A or Z from each index (ABCBAC, Erase and Extend, Compress String) replaces nested string compares when n≤10^6.

tradeoffs.topic: KMP automaton DP vs plain “run KMP”
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When counting/forbidding/requiring a pattern inside built strings, keep state = current π match length with alphabet transitions (Required Substring, Lucky Common Subsequence, Obsessive String).

tradeoffs.topic: Reverse trie + end DP vs forward dictionary scan
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For Spy Syndrome 2, store dictionary words reversed and DP from the ciphertext end so walking the trie forward matches a word ending here.

tradeoffs.topic: Run-length block KMP vs character-level KMP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: On Messenger, compress (c,len) blocks; match interior blocks exactly and treat first/last as prefix/suffix length constraints.

tradeoffs.topic: Binary trie XOR counts vs max-only XOR
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For XOR ≥ k subarray counts, walk bit-by-bit and add whole subtrees when the bit choice already satisfies the threshold — same structure as Vasiliy, different query.
Color with Occurrences can greedily / DP-cover t with given patterns as substrings — multi-pattern matching without needing full Aho.

gotchas.trap: Solving one-deletion / Hamming-1 membership with full edit distance.
gotchas.correction: Fix the dropped or mismatched position (or branch once in a trie) and verify flanks with O(1) prefix/suffix hashes.

gotchas.trap: Accepting all forced starts of p without checking overlaps.
gotchas.correction: An overlap is legal iff p’s border chain / period divides the gap; then free cells contribute 26^cnt.

gotchas.trap: Inserting dictionary words forward for reverse-decode tasks.
gotchas.correction: Store words reversed; DP from the end of the ciphertext while walking the trie forward.

gotchas.trap: Expanding even-split equivalence into concrete rearrangements.
gotchas.correction: Hash both half-orders and recurse; do not expand into O(n) copies.

gotchas.trap: Using a max-XOR binary trie for “XOR ≥ k” counts.
gotchas.correction: Walk bits and add whole subtree counts when the threshold is already satisfied (Beautiful Subarrays).

gotchas.trap: Character-level KMP on run-length compressed text/pattern.
gotchas.correction: KMP on (c,len) blocks: exact middle matches, ends as prefix/suffix length constraints (Messenger).
Use Z or hashing (Message Transmission hard, Erase and Extend, Compress String, ABCBAC).

gotchas.trap: Reaching for full Aho when covering a string by dictionary substrings.
gotchas.correction: Greedy / DP-cover with the given patterns as substrings can suffice (Color with Occurrences).
